extractedBy: Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5), Penny run run_19b90d38, extraction worker
notes: Extracted from the guide and evidence at e7ed622 on the installed build: jfs-components 0.1.78, mirror tag v0.1.78-dbe0e02 (Biscuit's main at dbe0e02, 27 October 2026), the build the guide's Sources were checked on (28 October). Where the evidence's older sections (Contract, Accessibility, the #234 'still open' list) disagree with its dbe0e02 section or the package types, the newer ones were used: focus is moved in, kept in and returned; Escape closes the sheet from the text field too; the scrim calls onRequestClose when onOverlayPress is omitted; and 'with the drag off the sheet never calls onRequestClose' no longer holds, since Escape calls it. The guide names no other component to use instead: 'a new flow deserves its own screen' means an app screen, not the Screen component, so the avoidWhen rule has no useInstead. The examples are the guide's own slot content (an AppBar with JioDot and a Close IconButton, the one line of Text, a VStack spacer when the sheet fills the screen, and a HelloJioInput), without the guide's Color Mode Light, the close IconButton's Emphasis Low (no guide copy says that content needs it), Page type MainPage and fillHeight true (both defaults), and without presentationProgress and the page-stack hook, which need a shared value from the screen. The guide's own App Bar has no title, so its dialogs are unnamed; the examples keep it that way rather than invent one. Refreshed 29 October 2026 for guide fix #543 (3f56271): the evidence now calls the HelloJio Input's surface its field; the gap quotes the new sentence and /configuration/12 and the gap say field in their own words.

configuration.text: Set visible to present the sheet over the page; the screen shows and hides it. Without visible, the sheet renders in place as a plain surface.
Wire onRequestClose to set visible to false: it reports that people asked to close the sheet (a drag down), and the screen hides it.
By default (fillHeight true) the sheet covers the screen and the field sits at its foot.

from.quote: The default: the sheet covers the screen and the field sits at its foot.

configuration.text: With showOverlay, set onOverlayPress to hide the sheet when the scrim is pressed; when it's omitted, the scrim calls onRequestClose if that is set.

configuration.text: Put the AppBar and the HelloJioInput straight in the slot (or in a fragment), not inside a component of your own: the sheet adjusts only the children it can see, so under Page type JioPlus a nested AppBar shows white on the grey sheet and a nested HelloJioInput's field matches the sheet.

from.quote: The sheet does this only for children it can see: its direct slot children, fragments, and their `children` props.

absolute.reason: "only" limits which slot children the sheet adjusts under Page type (direct children, fragments and their children), not what may go in the slot.

evidenceFacts.name: modes
evidenceFacts.description: The sheet passes its modes to its slot children without Page type (an AppBar keeps it) and without Color Mode Dark; a child's own modes are merged over them.
evidenceFacts.quote: Since c1fa197 (#255) the sheet drops Page type (and Color Mode Dark) from the modes it passes to slot children, except an AppBar, which keeps Page type; a child's own modes are still merged over them.

evidenceFacts.name: children
evidenceFacts.description: The sheet adjusts only the slot children it can see: its direct children, fragments, and their children props. An AppBar or HelloJioInput rendered inside a consumer's own component isn't recognised.
evidenceFacts.quote: The sheet does this only for children it can see: its direct slot children, fragments, and their `children` props.

evidenceFacts.name: visible
evidenceFacts.description: With visible set, the sheet fills its nearest positioned parent as an overlay, and visible false keeps it mounted below the screen. It is not a Modal or portal: the screen sets visible to false on every close.
evidenceFacts.quote: It is not a Modal or portal; the screen sets `visible` to false on every close.

evidenceFacts.name: topInset
evidenceFacts.description: With fillHeight false the sheet docks to the bottom and ignores the inset; with fillHeight it shortens by the inset so its bottom stays on the screen.
evidenceFacts.quote: With `fillHeight={false}` it docks to the bottom and ignores the inset.

evidenceFacts.name: trapFocus
evidenceFacts.description: With trapFocus false, Escape doesn't close the sheet, and a sheet shown from the first render leaves focus on the page; with the default, a sheet shown at load still takes focus.
evidenceFacts.quote: With `trapFocus={false}` Escape doesn't close the sheet.

evidenceFacts.name: enableDismissGesture
evidenceFacts.description: Gates only the drag and its “Drag down to dismiss” hint; the scrim and a close button in the slot still work.
evidenceFacts.quote: The scrim (`onOverlayPress`) and a close button in the slot still work

evidenceFacts.name: accessibilityLabel
evidenceFacts.description: Names the dialog; without it, a slot child's title names it.
evidenceFacts.quote: `accessibilityLabel` (names the dialog; else a slot child's `title` prop)

evidenceFacts.name: Page type
evidenceFacts.description: MainPage and SubPage give a white sheet (#ffffff), JioPlus a light grey one (#f5f5f5).

gaps.text: Under Page type JioPlus, an AppBar or HelloJioInput rendered inside a consumer's own component in the slot isn't recognised: the AppBar loses Page type (white on the grey sheet) and the HelloJioInput's field isn't repainted, so it still matches the sheet. The #255 fix doesn't reach them; the evidence leaves this limit for Marcin to judge.
gaps.quote: an AppBar or a HelloJio Input it renders inside isn't recognised: the AppBar loses Page type (white on the grey sheet) and the field isn't repainted, so it still matches the sheet.

gaps.text: A hidden sheet sets inert as the string "true", so React 19 logs a development warning; the sheet still works (#417, Component Bug, To do).
gaps.quote: a hidden sheet sets `inert="true"` as a string, so React 19 logs “Received the string `true` for the boolean attribute `inert`” in development
